# 廣百論本

**Category:** 中觀部類

**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 650
**Juans:** 1

## Contributors
- 聖天 (A001207)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Tang-period translation by [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) 玄奘 (602–664) of the *kārikā*-text of the latter half of Āryadeva's *Catuḥśataka* "Four-Hundred Verses" — specifically the eight "śāstra" chapters (the so-called *yogācāra-saptaka* + the polemical chapters) that constitute the second half of the 400-verse work. The first half (the *bodhisattva-saptaka*, on the cultivation of merit and knowledge by the bodhisattva) was not separately translated into Chinese. T1570 supplies the verses alone; the verses with [護法菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%B7%E6%B3%95%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dharmapāla)'s prose commentary are translated separately as [KR6m0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0015) *Dàshèng guǎngbǎi lùn shìlùn* 大乘廣百論釋論 (T1571). Translated at Cháng'ān in the early 650s as part of the Xuánzàng translation programme; the colophon dates the work to Yǒnghuī 永徽 1 (650).

**Abstract**

The *Catuḥśataka* of Āryadeva is the principal Mādhyamaka treatise after the *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* and the foundational text for the second wave of Chinese Mādhyamaka transmission under Xuánzàng. T1570 preserves the verses (160 quatrains, eight chapters of twenty stanzas each) of the second half of the work in Xuánzàng's characteristic literary-Chinese rendering — terse, line-by-line, using the four-character verse form. The Sanskrit original of T1570 is partially preserved (in the form of citations in Candrakīrti's *Catuḥśatakaṭīkā*, in fragments recovered by Haraprasad Shastri in 1914, and in the more recent finds of Shastri Sankrityayan and others); the Tibetan translation by Pa-tshab is preserved as Tōh. 3846. T1570 is therefore one of three major textual witnesses to the *Catuḥśataka*'s second half.

T1570 was used in Tang-period exegetical practice as the *kārikā*-only edition for memorisation and recitation, with [KR6m0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0015) T1571 supplying the verses with Dharmapāla's prose commentary on chapters 9–16. The two texts are normally bound together in East-Asian Buddhist canon-compilations and treated as a single work.
